implementation_notes: The everyday JavaScript idiom is a factory function: createOrder(raw) validates raw data, closes over any private state it needs and returns a plain object, so the classic class hierarchy is not written at all - MDN's class guide notes that a class is largely a createX factory function once shared methods are wanted. Nothing in the language can hide a constructor, so the replacement for constructor privacy is closure state, #private fields or Object.freeze, and the replacement for a factory class is a module-level function exported as the creation API. Reach for Object.create or class only when prototype-shared methods, instanceof checks or subclassing matter; a factory function remains the entry point that hides them.
pitfalls: A factory returning a mutable object abandons its invariants at the first caller assignment; freeze the result or hide state behind closures/#private fields.
instanceof and class checks break when the factory returns plain objects or switches implementation; document the structural interface instead.
Passing JSON.parse output straight through a function called createX, with no field validation, only creates the appearance of a boundary.
